## Agenda {.divider-slide}

Use this slide as a **table of contents**. Bold items indicate the current section.
Active items are highlighted; others are dimmed automatically.

1. **Introduction**
2. Methodology
3. Results
4. Discussion
5. Summary & Outlook

## Section Break {.divider-slide}

Use this slide as a **section break** between major topics.
It provides a visual pause and signals the transition to the next chapter.

## Content Slide {.content-slide}

### Use this layout for text-heavy content

Use this slide to present key information as a bullet list.
A subtitle (h3) can be added below the slide title to provide additional context.

- First bullet point with a key statement
- Second bullet point with supporting detail
- Third bullet point with nested sub-items
  - Sub-item A
  - Sub-item B
- Fourth bullet point as a summary or conclusion

## Two-Column Content {.content-slide}

Use this layout to **compare two topics** or present parallel information side by side.
Each column can contain text, lists, images, or code.

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}
### Left Column
- First point on the left side
- Second point with detail
- Third supporting argument
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
### Right Column
- Corresponding point on the right
- Contrasting or complementary detail
- Conclusion or comparison
:::

::::

## Boxed Content {.content-box-slide}

Use this layout to place content inside a **white rounded box**.
Suitable for longer paragraphs, tables, code blocks, or embedded visuals
that benefit from a clear visual boundary.

::: {.content-box}
Place your content here — text, tables, images, or other elements.

The white box visually separates the content from the slide background
and helps guide the reader's focus.
:::

::: {.split-right}

:::

## Argument Slide {.argument-slide}

### AI changed the economics of code production. The quality loop has to change with it.

<div class="argument-lead">
Use this pattern when you need to frame a shift in conditions, then explain what
the audience should do differently.
</div>

<div class="argument-grid">
<div class="argument-card argument-card--tension">

### Why the old signal breaks

- The context changed
- Old heuristics are no longer enough
- The failure mode is now hidden deeper in the workflow

<div class="argument-gap">
<div class="argument-gap__label">Tension</div>
<div>Everything looks fine until the untested edge case appears.</div>
</div>

</div>

<div class="argument-card argument-card--response">

### What the audience needs instead

- Faster feedback
- More specific signals
- A tighter loop between diagnosis and action

<div class="argument-note">
This works best for narrative slides that explain why a new operating model is required.
</div>

</div>
</div>
